To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
multifunctional ligands can be used to tune the redox potential of a metal center and that this allows for facile access to high metal oxidation states.
we have designed a family of ruthenium catalysts for the oxidation of water that are capable of performing the water oxidation reaction in the presence of a sacrificial oxidant at pH 7.
multifunctional ligands are able to tune redox-potentials and activation barriers in a single-site water oxidation catalyst.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel ruthenium complexes for catalytic water oxidation, which are based on a multifunctional bidentate ligand.
the design and synthesis of new ruthenium complexes incorporating multifunctional biphosphonate bipyridyl ligands.
the development and mechanistic understanding of new water-oxidation catalysts that are based on ruthenium complexes incorporating multifunctional biphosphonic acid ligands.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we are now able to rationally design catalysts for water oxidation that are fast, robust, and stable, and which can work under neutral conditions.
the use of phosphonate groups in the design of water oxidation catalysts is a very promising strategy for the design of catalysts that operate at neutral pH.
the phosphonate group in these complexes plays an important dual role in water oxidation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have designed a family of water oxidation catalysts that have the potential to operate in a broad range of pH conditions and that are capable of oxidizing water at rates comparable to those of the best homogeneous and heterogeneous catalysts.
the multifunctional phosphonate ligands provide a means to control the oxidation states and protonation states of the catalyst and thus the reaction mechanism.
the multifunctional ligands are a key factor to achieve high catalytic performance in water oxidation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the incorporation of phosphonate groups in a bipyridine ligand can provide a unique combination of electronic and steric properties that can be exploited for the development of efficient and selective catalysts for water oxidation.
the incorporation of multifunctional phosphonate groups into the ligands of Ru complexes can lead to highly active catalysts for water oxidation.
the multifunctional ligands provide the necessary charge compensation for high-oxidation-state complexes and facilitate the proton-coupled electron transfer processes.
